introduction: The protocol aims to guide a future review of the effects of aerobic exercise on reducing depression levels in adults. The authors note that many existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses have methodological limitations that prevent definitive conclusions.
methodology: A protocol for a systematic review with meta-analysis of aerobic exercise for depression in adults, following PRISMA-P 2020. Searches will cover BVS, Cochrane library, Embase, Epistemonikos, PubMed and SPORTDiscus. Risk of bias will be assessed with RoB 2.0 and certainty with GRADE.
results: The paper is a protocol and reports no results.
discussion: The authors expect the review to identify the effective dose-response to reduce depression levels and to provide an understanding of the mechanisms through which aerobic exercise influences depression. They also expect it to specify which intensities, frequencies and durations produce the most favorable outcomes.
limitations: The authors anticipate limitations including small sample sizes, a lack of clarity about mechanisms, variation in intensity protocols, and high heterogeneity among studies. A narrative synthesis will discuss research gaps for future investigations.

introduction.q: This protocol proposal aims to guide a future systematic review that will seek to answer the following question: what are the effects of aerobic exercise on reducing depression levels in adults?
However, many existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses have methodological limitations that prevent definitive conclusions.

methodology.q: This article presents a protocol for conducting a systematic review with meta-analysis
which will follow the PRISMA-P 2020 guidelines
The search will be conducted in the following databases: BVS, Cochrane library, Embase, Epistemonikos, PubMed and SPORTDiscus.
the risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 method
The certainty of evidence will be evaluated through the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).

results.q: This is a systematic review protocol
The study is a protocol for a systematic review, which will follow the guidelines developed by Page et al.

discussion.q: identify the effective dose-response to reduce depression levels and provide an understanding of the mechanisms through which aerobic exercise influences depression
specifying which intensities, frequencies, and durations of aerobic exercise produce the most favorable outcomes

limitations.q: Anticipated limitations and challenges include the following issues: the use of small sample sizes, lack of clarity regarding the specific mechanisms through which exercise contributes to the improvement of depression, and variations in the intensity protocols adopted.
one of the main methodological challenges expected in the conduction of this review is the high heterogeneity among the studies to be included
a narrative synthesis will discuss the clinical implications of the findings, the limitations of the included studies, and the research gaps that need to be addressed in future investigations.

abstract_claims.q: Studies suggest that aerobic exercise can improve mental health and reduce depression symptoms, despite variations in exercise type and intensity.

It is expected that the systematic review following this protocol will identify the effective dose-response to reduce depression levels and provide an understanding of the mechanisms through which aerobic exercise influences depression.

caveats.q: Eligible study types will be randomized clinical trials (RCTs)
excluding individuals with chronic degenerative diseases or other associated severe psychiatric disorders
Only studies utilizing validated depression assessment scales will be included
while ongoing clinical trials with preliminary results will be excluded

studies involving populations with non-communicable chronic diseases (e.g., hypertension, diabetes), case reports, preprints, narrative and systematic reviews, and observational studies will not be considered for inclusion
the most widely used scale (i.e., the Hamilton Scale) will be prioritized
which will be generated only if at least 10 studies are included in the meta-analysis
Studies with a high risk of bias will be identified, considering the worst judgment in any of the assessed domains, excluding blinding domains due to the nature of physical exercise interventions.
However, these guidelines do not provide clear and consistent recommendations regarding the dose or modality of exercise
However, many existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses have methodological limitations that prevent definitive conclusions.
Furthermore, the underlying mechanisms of these effects are still not fully understood
However, the findings did not allow for the precise establishment of a dose-response relationship due to variability in the study protocols analyzed
Although exercise is not yet considered an essential component on its own
which may have limited the results
The systematic review studies conducted so far, although following rigorous methodologies and providing relevant contributions to the scientific field, present some methodological limitations.
However, this review aims precisely to highlight these issues and deepen the understanding of their implications.
